paragraphs: Rav Acha bar Rav, Menachot 3b; Rav Mesharshya’s paternal grandfather, chapter Hannisrafin 77a. Rosh writes he was our holy master’s colleague (an error for the early Ravina). Under Rav Acha bar Natan, Yuchasin writes that Rav Acha bar Natan and Mar Zutra bar Rav Mari spoke to Ravina; he was the grandfather—that is, Rav Acha was Rav Mesharshya’s paternal grandfather, in Rava’s time, as in Ellu Tereifot. Likewise Rosh, Hannisrafin, says Rav Mesharshya, Rava’s student, was Rav Acha’s grandson, and Rav Acha disputed with the early Ravina. End quotation. See Ellu Tereifot 49a: a lung was punctured where the butcher’s hand handles it—do we attribute the puncture to that handling? Rav Acha bar Natan says yes; Mar Zutra son of Rav Mari says no. Rav Mesharshya says his paternal grandfather’s view (Rashi: Rav Acha) is reasonable, since we attribute it to a wolf. Asheri reads Rav Acha bar Rava; Rif reads Rav Acha bar Yaakov. See Asheri, beginning of Hannisrafin: Ravina finds liable, Rav Acha bar Rav exempts, etc.; Rav Mesharshya asks his grandfather’s reason. “I think this Ravina is not the one in Rav Ashi’s days. This Rav Acha is not Ravina’s usual disputant, but an early one, son of Rav and paternal grandfather of Rav Mesharshya, who is Rav’s student; both were early amoraim.” End quotation. (See the early Ravina.) See Yuchasin’s error: Rav Acha bar Rav should be read, and he was Rav’s student; likewise correct the Gemara, Asheri in Ellu Tereifot, and Alfasi. Yuchasin’s “they spoke to Ravina” is absent from Ellu Tereifot, though each is found speaking to Ravina elsewhere. You will find no Rav Acha bar Natan throughout the Talmud; that occurrence is a scribal error. Only Mar Zutra bar Rav Mari is found speaking to Ravina. He needlessly gave Rav Acha bar Natan a separate entry, for the only mention is there, truly an error. (See Abba, Rav’s father.) Eruvin 90b: Rav Achi son of Rav should read Acha. Rav Acha bar Rav sent to Ravina, who replied, “You who heard what Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua said.”
Because errors commonly confuse Rabbi Acha bar Rav and Rabbi Acha bar Rava, I placed them adjoining, where they can be compared.
